questions.topic: Nature, concept and general principles of intellectual property
questions.ideal_answer: Intellectual property refers to creations of the human mind, such as inventions, literary and artistic works, software, designs, symbols, names and images used in commerce. Intellectual property rights are legal rights that give the creator or owner exclusive control over the use of their creation for a limited period. They encourage innovation and creativity by allowing creators to benefit financially. The main forms are patents, copyrights, trademarks, industrial designs and geographical indications.

A patent is an exclusive right granted by the government to an inventor for an invention that is new, involves an inventive step and is capable of industrial application. It allows the owner to stop others from making, using, selling or importing the invention without permission. In exchange, the inventor must publicly disclose the details of the invention. In India and under TRIPS a patent lasts for 20 years from the date of filing.

questions.topic: Forms of IP: copyright, patent, trademark, design, geographical indication
questions.text: What is the difference between a copyright and a trademark? Give an example of each.
questions.ideal_answer: A copyright protects original creative expression, such as books, music, films and software code, and arises automatically when the work is created. A trademark protects a sign, logo, word or symbol that distinguishes the goods or services of one business from others. For example, the source code of an app is protected by copyright, while the app's name and logo, like the Swiggy logo, can be protected as a trademark. Copyright lasts for a fixed term, while a trademark can be renewed indefinitely, every 10 years in India.

questions.topic: Semiconductor layout designs and plant varieties
questions.text: What is protected under semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design law?
questions.ideal_answer: Layout-design law protects the original three-dimensional arrangement of transistors and other elements and interconnections in a semiconductor integrated circuit. It does not protect the electronic function or the underlying idea, only the specific layout. In India this is covered by the Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Act, 2000, and the layout must be original and not commercially exploited before. Registration gives protection for 10 years and prevents others from copying or commercially using the layout.

questions.text: How does a geographical indication work? Explain with an Indian example.
questions.ideal_answer: A geographical indication is a sign used on products that come from a specific geographical location and possess qualities or a reputation due to that origin. Producers in that region can register the GI, and then only authorised users from that area can use the name. For example, Darjeeling Tea was India's first registered GI, so tea grown outside the Darjeeling region cannot be sold as Darjeeling Tea. In India GIs are governed by the Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999, and registration is valid for 10 years and renewable.

questions.text: A startup wants to protect its brand name and logo. How should it go about registering a trademark in India?
questions.ideal_answer: The startup should first do a trademark search to make sure the name and logo are distinctive and not similar to existing registered marks. It then files an application with the Trade Marks Registry in the correct class of goods or services under the Trade Marks Act, 1999. The application is examined, published in the Trade Marks Journal for opposition, and registered if there is no successful opposition. Registration lasts 10 years and can be renewed indefinitely, and the registered mark can use the R symbol.

questions.text: Why is software 'as such' generally not patentable in India, and when can a software-related invention be patented?
questions.ideal_answer: Section 3(k) of the Indian Patents Act excludes mathematical methods, business methods, computer programs per se and algorithms from patentability. This is because pure code is treated as an abstract idea, which is already protected by copyright as a literary work. A computer-related invention can be patented if it shows a technical effect or technical contribution, for example software combined with novel hardware or that improves the functioning of a device. It must still be novel, inventive and industrially applicable.

questions.text: Compare the Paris Convention and the Berne Convention.
questions.ideal_answer: The Paris Convention of 1883 deals with industrial property such as patents, trademarks, industrial designs and geographical indications. Its key principles are national treatment and the right of priority, which gives an applicant 12 months for patents and 6 months for trademarks and designs to file in other member countries using the first filing date. The Berne Convention of 1886 deals with copyright in literary and artistic works. Its key principles are national treatment and automatic protection without any registration formalities, with a minimum term of life of the author plus 50 years.

questions.text: How does the TRIPS Agreement differ from earlier WIPO-administered treaties in enforcing IP rights?
questions.ideal_answer: The WIPO Convention of 1967 created the World Intellectual Property Organization, which administers treaties like Paris and Berne but has weak enforcement mechanisms. The TRIPS Agreement of 1994 is part of the World Trade Organization and links IP protection to international trade. It sets minimum standards for all forms of IP, including protecting computer programs as literary works and a 20-year patent term. Crucially, disputes under TRIPS can be taken to the WTO dispute settlement mechanism, which can authorise trade sanctions, making it much more enforceable.

questions.text: A developer copies a competitor's app idea but writes all the code from scratch. Is this copyright infringement? Explain.
questions.ideal_answer: Generally no, because copyright protects the expression of an idea and not the idea itself, which is called the idea-expression dichotomy. If the code is written independently and is not substantially similar to the original source code, there is usually no infringement. However, copying protected expressive elements such as the exact user interface graphics, text, icons or substantial code structure could still infringe. The idea itself could be protected only by a patent if it qualifies, or by keeping it as a trade secret.

questions.topic: IP management, IP audit and remedies for infringement
questions.text: You are joining an IT startup as a tech lead. How would you manage and protect the company's intellectual property?
questions.ideal_answer: I would first conduct an IP audit to identify all IP assets such as source code, algorithms, brand names, designs and data, and check who owns them. Employment and contractor agreements should include IP assignment and confidentiality clauses so the company owns work created for it. The brand should be registered as a trademark, patentable technical inventions should be filed early, and sensitive algorithms kept as trade secrets with access control. I would also check open-source licence compliance and monitor for infringement, using legal remedies such as cease-and-desist notices, injunctions and damages if needed.

questions.topic: IP management, IP audit and remedies for infringement
questions.text: Your company discovers that another firm is selling a cracked version of your software. What remedies are available and what steps would you take?
questions.ideal_answer: This is copyright infringement and software piracy, and may also be an offence under the Copyright Act and the IT Act. The first steps are to collect evidence such as download links and copies, and send a cease-and-desist notice and takedown requests to hosting platforms. Civil remedies include an injunction to stop the sale, damages or an account of profits, and seizure of infringing copies. Criminal remedies under the Copyright Act include imprisonment and fines, and the company should also strengthen licensing checks and anti-piracy measures.
